claims.proposition_evaluated: At its meeting of 2026-08-26 the Infrastructure Committee rejected administration's recommended hold on the remaining programme routes (Recommendation 1 of IS03688, R) rather than adopting it, and City Council had not adopted the hold by 2026-09-25. 'Hold' means claim 2's primary deferral definition.
claims.interpretation_notes: Verdict unchanged from round 1: Partially supported. The committee left R without a decision, no body adopted R, and the declared primary version of R did not propose a hold. (1) Treatment. The agenda and minutes list all three versions of Attachment 5 but do not say which was before the committee, so the brief's declared primary applies: Version 2 (304030). Version 2 says 'The remaining routes will be evaluated for trade-offs, alternative design treatments and budget implications', with a Q1 2027 report 'for Council direction and approval'. It does not say that the listed routes wait for that step, so it is not a hold under the primary definition. The treatment it proposes, in its own words, is that the 14 projects 'may be re-evaluated using alternate design approaches'. The original (304032) is a hold: the projects 'would be removed from the scope ... for 2026 and 2027' and may be revisited after evaluation. Version 1 (304031) is also a hold on my reading, because unbuilt routes 'would be evaluated to determine if they should proceed'. The verdict is the same under every version, because the disposition is identical: the committee left R without a decision. Under Version 2 that is the no-hold row; under the original and Version 1 it is the hold row. Only the reason changes. (2) Disposition at item 7.6 (minutes, item 7.6). Councillor Salvador moved to 'Continue implementation ... in accordance with the previously approved scope of Capital Profile CM-20-0330', to advance tender-ready routes and to prepare procurement for 2027. Councillor Rutherford moved an amendment to delete 'and maximize remaining construction season, including advancing partial and accelerated construction' from Part 2. The amendment was defeated 2 to 2 (for: Rutherford, Clarke; against: Salvador, Janz). The motion, put, was defeated 2 to 2 (for: Salvador, Janz; against: Rutherford, Clarke). Recommendation 2 (Attachment 4 to remain private), moved by Rutherford, carried 4 to 0 (Rutherford, Salvador, Clarke, Janz). The procedural motions were to meet in private (moved by Clarke, carried 5 to 0, with Knack voting) and to meet in public (moved by Rutherford, carried 5 to 0, with Paquette voting). Committee members entitled to vote were Rutherford, Salvador, Clarke, Janz, Paquette and, ex officio under section 15(3) of Bylaw 18156, Mayor Knack. Knack and Paquette are not recorded on the amendment or the substantive motion. Paquette was 'absent with notice for a portion of the meeting'. Elliott, Morgan, Parmar, Principe, Stevenson, Tang and Wright attended as non-members. No motion to adopt R was moved or put, and no motion incompatible with R was carried. Every substantive motion failed, which is the brief's own example of leaving R without a decision. (3) Required alternative reading ('did not support' means non-adoption): Supported. (4) Required alternative body, City Council: Not established. R was not before Council by 2026-09-25. At Council on 2026-09-08 (continued 2026-09-16), the only item carried under the selection rule, which covers the terms IS03688, CM-20-0330 and 'bike', is item 11.6. That is Salvador's notice of motion on options to increase CM-20-0330 funding in the 2027–2030 budget, and it was laid over to 2026-10-06. At Executive Committee on 2026-09-02 (item 10.1), the pending motion could not be made 'due to time constraints' and was restated as a notice. Neither item is R. (5) Override: none is shown. The committee made no decision on item 7.6 incompatible with R, beyond defeating motions and keeping Attachment 4 private. No later, incompatible Council decision is recorded. The absence of a later Council item is an absence, not an override and not agreement. (6) What governed after 2026-08-26: the previously approved CM-20-0330 profile ($100,000,000; Capital Budget Amendment 7 as restated, carried 9 to 4 in the 2022 budget), together with Council's 2026-07-07 decision to rescope 50 Street. No later Council decision appears in the carried record. In statements that are administration's, not Council decisions, the report says 'for routes where construction has not yet started, construction is best postponed to 2027'. Attachment 3 says six routes' 'installation in 2026 is no longer viable ... Next steps for these segments will depend on Council's direction', and its footnote 2 says the tendered routes 'may be delayed ... or removed ... pending this Council report'. These statements are not part of R and do not make R a hold. (7) Self-correction: in round 1 I cited Global News and Taproot. Both were checked in round 2 and are withdrawn as evidence. The Global headline calls the committee's action a 'city council' rejection. Taproot says councillors 'received the report for information', which 'left the previously approved expansion program in place'. The minutes record no motion to receive for information, and the motion to continue the previously approved scope was defeated. Both are leads only, and neither matches the minutes' language.

claims.proposition_evaluated: In IS03688 for the Infrastructure Committee of 2026-08-26, administration recommended an approach that expressly defers construction or advancement of 14 named, unbuilt programme routes until a further evaluation, report or decision.
claims.interpretation_notes: Verdict unchanged from round 1: Partially supported under the declared primary (Version 2, 304030). Recommendation 1 asks for approval of the Attachment 5 approach. Version 2 lists 14 routes apart, and all 14 were unbuilt on 2026-08-10. It fails the primary deferral reading: evaluation and a Q1 2027 report, with no statement that the routes wait. It also fails the stricter reading, since it contains no removal or 'will not proceed' language. Lists (identical in all three versions). Continuing, 13 entries: 50 Street (109A Avenue to Goldbar Park Road); 84 Avenue (Mill Creek Ravine to 91 Street); 100 Street (76 Avenue to 80 Avenue); 107 Avenue (East of Groat Road to 163 Street); 110 Avenue/90 Street (92 Street to 112 Avenue) and 112 Avenue (90 Street to 76 Street); 111 Avenue (120 Street to 121 Street); 114 Avenue (81 Street to 89 Street); 127 Avenue (97 Street to 102A Street); 163 Street from 87 Avenue to 95 Avenue; 163 Street (Stony Plain Road to 107 Avenue); 167 Street/169 Street (Whitemud Drive to 87 Avenue); Kingsway (113 Street to 122 Street); Victoria Park Road (116 Street to River Valley Road). Listed apart, 14 entries, with statuses from Attachment 3 as of 2026-08-10: 50 Street (101 Avenue to 109A Avenue), 'Other', no delivery plan, 'paused for reconsideration' (footnote 1); 64 Street (119 Avenue to Yellowhead Trail), 'installation in 2026 is no longer viable'; 79 Street (76 Avenue to 101 Avenue), same; 84 Avenue (79 Street to 83 Street), 'Tender awarded. Construction has not yet started'; 85 Street (93 Avenue to 98 Avenue), no longer viable in 2026; 88 Avenue/93 Street/87 Avenue (85 Street to 96 Street), no longer viable in 2026; 89 Street (76 Avenue to Connors Road), no longer viable in 2026; 92A Avenue/86 Street/alley (Connors Road to 85 Street), tender awarded and not started; 93 Street (82 Avenue to 84 Avenue) and 84 Avenue (91 Street to 89 Street), which Attachment 3 lists as '93 Street/84 Avenue (89 Street to 82 Avenue)', tender awarded and not started; 93 Avenue/82 Street/94 Avenue (85 Street to 75 Street) and 75 Street (94 Avenue to 94B Avenue), no longer viable in 2026; 95 Avenue (142 Street to 163 Street), 101 Avenue (50 Street to west of 84 Street), 106 Avenue (50 Street to west of 84 Street) and Grovenor (148 Street, 104 Avenue and 144 Street segments), each 'Other', no delivery plan. None is recorded as under construction or complete. Count: 14 by bullet. Splitting the two 'and' entries and the three-segment Grovenor entry gives 18. The status at the alternative date of 2026-08-26 is unresolved for all 14, because no dated route-by-route City record for that date is available. The report's 2026-08-26 text says only that 'for routes where construction has not yet started, construction is best postponed to 2027'. Classification by version. Original (304032): the projects 'would be removed from the scope ... for 2026 and 2027', to be revisited after evaluation. That is Supported under both readings. Version 1 (304031): 'Routes that have not yet been constructed in 2026 ... would be evaluated to determine if they should proceed'. That meets the primary reading, so Supported under the primary. For the stricter reading, removal is stated only for routes that 'impact travel lanes' or 'parking', and the listed routes are not stated in terms to be such routes; the passage on the listed routes says they 'may be revisited'. That is Partially supported under the stricter reading. Here I disagree with gpt, which classed Version 1 as failing the primary reading. Version 2: Partially supported under both readings. The finding is version-sensitive, and the story must say so beside the verdict. Qualification 3: the report says the recommendations 'would not result in any changes required to the existing capital profile CM-20-0330 ... or associated borrowing bylaws'. Qualification 4: the recommendation was addressed to the Infrastructure Committee, to recommend to City Council, and was labelled 'Council decision required'. MATERIAL FRAMING CONCERN, with the claim answered as posed above. Version 2 says that routes whose plans do not affect travel lanes or parking 'will continue as planned', and that 'the remaining routes' will be evaluated and reported on in Q1 2027 'for Council direction and approval'. Read with the report's 'best postponed to 2027' and Attachment 3's footnote 2 ('may be delayed ... or removed ... pending this Council report'), the practical effect is that the 14 would not proceed as planned until Council gave direction. The brief's 'expressly' test excludes that implication, and that exclusion is what separates Partially supported from Supported. The story should say that Version 2 implies, but does not state, that the 14 wait. Taproot's lay summary ('reassessing 14 others') is a lead only.

claims.proposition_evaluated: Between the programme's approval in the 2022-11-30 budget deliberations and 2026-09-25, Councillors Karen Principe and Jennifer Rice brought two motions at City Council that sought to leave about $50 million (between $45 million and $55 million) in CM-20-0330, directed the released funds to named destinations, and were defeated by Council.
claims.interpretation_notes: Verdict unchanged from round 1: Partially supported. Two jointly brought reduction motions, on separate occasions, were both defeated. Only the first leaves about $50 million. Motion A: City Council Budget, November 2023 sessions (21, 22 and 27 November), item 5.1.2, Capital Budget Amendment 2 as restated. Moved by Principe, seconded by Rice: 'That capital profile CM-20-0330 - Active Transportation Implementation Acceleration - Approach 3 be reduced by $50,000,000 ($16,350,000 in 2024, $16,825,000 in 2025, and $16,825,000 in 2026) with a funding reduction from tax-supported debt.' For: Hamilton, Cartmell, Rice, Principe. Against: Knack, Paquette, Sohi, Salvador, Tang, Rutherford, Stevenson, Wright. Defeated 4 to 8. Janz is not recorded. The pre-restatement text said 'to go towards the tax levy', but the text put names a reduction in tax-supported debt, i.e. a reduction in borrowing. Motion B: City Council Budget, 2 and 3 December 2024 sessions, item 5.1.2, Capital Budget Amendment 2. Moved by Principe, seconded by Rice: 'decreased by $33,650,000 in 2025 and $33,650,000 in 2026 with funding from tax-supported debt, to defund planning, design and delivery'. For: Cartmell, Rice, Rutherford, Principe. Against: Knack, Sohi, Salvador, Janz, Tang, Stevenson, Wright. Defeated 4 to 7. Paquette was absent with notice, and Hamilton is not recorded. Its destination wording names the funding source being cut rather than a destination for the released funds. I accept it as a reduction in borrowing, but it is weaker than Motion A's. Base: $100,000,000, approved in the 2022 budget as Capital Budget Amendment 7 restated, carried 9 to 4. The base is corroborated in two ways. Motion B's two cuts equal exactly the original profile's 2025 and 2026 amounts ($33,650,000 each). And in 2026 administration still described '$100 million' approved and said no change to the profile was required. I could not verify gpt's 2024 financial update (DocumentId 245911, HTTP 403). The capital profile attachments and the approved SCBA adjustments for Spring 2023, Fall 2023 and Spring 2024 were not in the package. Reviewer's arithmetic. A: $100,000,000 − $50,000,000 = $50,000,000, inside the $45–55M band; the cut is 50% of the base, which meets 'at least half'. B: $33,650,000 × 2 = $67,300,000; $100,000,000 − $67,300,000 = $32,700,000, outside the band; the cut is 67.3%, which meets 'at least half'. For B's remainder to fall in the band, the base would have to be between $112,300,000 and $122,300,000, and nothing in the record suggests that. Alternative readings. Required alternative amount rule: Supported, provided Motion B's destination wording is accepted, otherwise Partially supported. Co-sponsorship alternative: the same as the primary, since Principe moved and Rice seconded both. The finding is therefore definition-sensitive on the amount band. Destinations: neither motion redirects funds to other 'core priorities', as the holder's words suggest. Both reduce debt funding. The carried 2026 Council and committee attendance lists do not include J. Rice. The brief describes the commenter as a sitting councillor, but the minutes do not bear that out for 2026. claims.suggested_short_answer: The minutes show that Councillor Principe moved and Councillor Rice seconded two cuts to the $100 million programme, and Council defeated both. The November 2023 motion (defeated 4–8) cut $50 million, leaving $50 million. The December 2024 motion (defeated 4–7) cut $67.3 million, leaving $32.7 million (reviewer's calculation). Both reduced the programme's debt funding rather than redirecting money to other priorities. 'Twice' holds; 'twice to $50M' holds only once.
